at: N6.5 done and closed: IPv6 is the kernel's (addresses, MLD, source selection, neighbour discovery, the output and input paths, forwarding, reassembly, ICMPv6, the protocol table), measured against its start (IPv6 delivery 54 % faster, reassembly 47 %) and tested; N6.5e done in three parts: the net lock's cells in `hal`, counted interface addresses and counted multicast records, freed when the last holder lets go as in OpenBSD; N6.6a, TCP, under way in six parts (6a0..6a5), built beside the old one and switched on last: all six are done: since 6a5 the kernel's TCP is the one that runs, and the old one is deleted; N6.6b done: UDP (6b0), raw sockets and divert (6b1) are the kernel's; N6.7a done: the nfs client is the kernel's (wire format, RPC engine, node table, attribute cache, diskless boot, file operations, mount; N6.7a0..a5) and the one that runs, the old client deleted; N6.7b done: pf's tables and IPsec's policies run on the kernel's radix tree (bsd's deleted), and the nfs server is the kernel's (nfssvc native, bsd's sys/nfs deleted); N6.8, the close, is next; a radix tree that owns its nodes and the NFS export list are the kernel's (N6.7b0); pf and IPsec on that tree (N6.7b1) and the server (N6.7b2, b3) are paused, partly written, until the client is done; `__thrsleep` and `__thrwakeup`, the thread sleep calls LandingZone ported, and `sysarch`, arrived by sync as safe kernel code: every LandingZone commit up to the new pin, e8249449, is triaged

slices.what: Preconditions in `hal`: the net lock (shared and exclusive, with witnesses), SMR for lock-free reads, pools with their own page allocator, typed in-place header views, a list with an O(1) tail; the network benchmarks
The mbuf, the packet buffer under everything (`uipc_mbuf`, `uipc_mbuf2`, `sys/mbuf.rs`)
Sockets and domains: the socket layer, local (AF_UNIX) sockets, descriptor passing; the socket system calls handled natively
The interface core: `ifnet`, the interface queues, `netisr`, link-level addresses and media
Routing: the routing table, ART, the routing socket
Link layers and bpf: Ethernet, loopback, the packet filter devices
IPv4 addresses and multicast records, IGMP, the IPv4 output path, the netinet header images and the IPv4 leaves (checksums, ids, ECN)
ARP, with the route's link-layer slot typed
The protocol control block shared by IPv4 and IPv6, and the IP socket options
The IPv4 input path, fragment reassembly, ICMP and the protocol table
IPv6 addresses and multicast records, MLD, source address selection, the IPv6 header images and leaves
Neighbour discovery (ND, duplicate address detection, the router cache)
The IPv6 output path and its socket options
The IPv6 input path, forwarding, fragment reassembly, ICMPv6, the extension headers and the protocol table
Cells the net lock guards in `hal`, opened by shared and exclusive witnesses, so a list under the net lock can lend its records safely
Counted interface addresses, IPv4 and IPv6: freed when the last holder lets go, as in OpenBSD, instead of recycled for ever
Counted multicast records, IPv4 and IPv6
TCP's preconditions: `hal` pieces (pool hard limit, arc4random_buf), the socket lock's shape, the pcb's typed slots, pf and IPsec legs
TCP without a control block: the state machine, sequence arithmetic, statistics per CPU, LRO and TSO
TCP's types, the control block's life, SACK and reassembly, the SYN cache
TCP output and its five timers
TCP input and the SYN cache's accept path
TCP's socket requests, options and sysctls; the switch to the kernel's TCP
UDP for IPv4 and IPv6, with IPsec's UDP checks and wg(4)'s upcall; the switch to the kernel's UDP
Raw IP, raw IPv6 and divert(4); the switch, the old files deleted
The nfs client's wire format: XDR encoding and decoding, the RPC transaction ids, the constants userland shares
The nfs client's types and its RPC engine (send, receive, retransmission timer), tested against a real socket on loopback
The nfs client's node table, attribute cache, kqueue support and the buffer cache's closed part
The nfs client's file operations (nfs_vnops) and the read and write paths
The nfs diskless boot (krpc, nfs_boot)
The switch to the kernel's nfs client; the old client deleted
A radix tree that owns its nodes, and the NFS export list; exports switched to the kernel
pf's tables and IPsec's policy lookup on the kernel's radix tree; the old tree deleted
The nfs server's core: its types, request cache, socket half and nfssvc's daemon loop
The nfs server's 26 procedures
The switch to the kernel's nfs server; nfssvc(2) handled natively
Close: `just check`, `just ci`, `just ci-full`, the comparison with a real OpenBSD (one new network scenario) green; the tag `n6-network`
